text: Pens and readers over FontGate ( fontgate.fg* ) layers and elements. Targets are an fgLayer or an fgShape (element), never an fgGlyph . Writing to a layer creates one new element for the pen session; writing to an element appends to it. Each contour is validated in Python first, then stored with a single contour.nodes = [...] assignment (point names and smooth flags kept). FontGate components are glyph-level only, so addComponent raises ComponentError . Empty native contours are never handed to native drawPoints , which dereferences the first node unchecked. The native fgPen fast path is not offered: it binds to a glyph's work shape, which conflicts with the layer/element rule.

text: Pens and readers over FontLab ( fontlab.fl* ) layers and elements. Targets are an flLayer or an flShape (element), never an flGlyph . Contours are staged and validated in Python; close() (or leaving the with block) writes them: a layer gets one new flShape holding all of them, an element gets them appended. On a layer, addComponent is staged too and close() adds the component elements and the contour shape in call order. An exception in the drawing body writes nothing; a native commit failure may leave partial geometry. The pen is spent even when a commit or notify fails. An element cannot hold components, and a component element cannot take contours. No undo history is recorded unless notify="title" is given for an attached layer. Notification can change unrelated native timestamps; whole-font history preservation is not guaranteed. Bare elements do not support notification.

text: Shared plan and write kernel of the anchor writer scripts. What: the Anchors scripts (Rename Bulk, Center Horizontally, Place From Bounds, Snap To Metrics, Round To Grid, Delete By Name, Mirror Across Masters) share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows. Each row can hold one Edit : ("set", name, (x, y)) : move the anchor; add it when it is missing; ("remove", name, None) : delete every anchor with this name; ("rename", name, new) : rename every anchor with this name. collect runs the planner on every editable layer and returns a Plan . require_safe refuses the whole batch before any history exists. apply_work writes all edits as ONE native Undo step and reads every value back. How: apply_work builds every native pin and point first ( prepare ), then calls fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit with operation="geometry" . The commit discloses queued native updates and refuses auto layers in the edit list, glyphs that own an auto layer and bases of auto composites (also through other composites). Then it inits history, runs write , stamps the glyphs, sends one notification and stamps again. unstored is the read-back: a value that FontLab did not keep raises RuntimeError . A failure after history started raises history.PartialWriteError ("... use Edit > Undo"). Why: FontLab cannot Redo an existing anchor moved to 0, 0 (FontLab issue 8527), so require_safe refuses that move. A new pin gets its name-derived appearance now ( anchor_copy.APPEARANCE ), because FontLab infers it only on Redo or reopen. An existing pin keeps its own style and expressions: write edits the existing pin object in place. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time. PythonQt, FontLab and anchor_copy load inside the functions, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. The panel base is in fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model . Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.anchors.panel.model as anchor_panel import fly.ap.anchors.writer as anchor_writer def planner(glyph, master, layer): return [anchor_writer.Change("top", "1, 2", "0, 2", ("set", "top", (0, 2)))] class Panel(anchor_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY = "Example", "anchors_example" def planner(self): return planner

text: Shared panel base and colour helpers of the anchor writer scripts. What: panel_type() returns AnchorPanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of the Anchors scripts: script controls, a live preview table, Reload selection, Close and Apply. ink , muted and readable_palette give readable text colours in FontLab's light and dark themes. How: the panel plans with fontlabapp.anchors.writer ( collect , blocked_rows , require_safe ) on every control change, and Apply plans again from live data and writes with anchor_writer.apply_work (one Undo step). text: Add plain components to EXISTING glyphs, inside the caller's one history step. What: a script that adds components to glyphs that exist (Make Lower Unicase, Set Default Figures) needs a new component shape for each (base glyph, layer). No component constructor is measured on this FontLab build (fl#8505: setGlyphComponents rejects every argument form, addComponent only records a recipe entry; the source has an flShape(glyph, layer) constructor, pyflshape.cpp:66-79 , which is a native probe item and is not used). Two calls: build_components(package, target, wanted, facts) , BEFORE the caller's history.commit . It clones one plain component that the font already has (the prototype), once per NewComponent , and points each detached clone at its base glyph, layer and offset. Nothing is added to the font yet. Refusals raise ValueError and name the target glyph, so a script can show a kept row: an unknown base, a base without that layer, a bad offset, and a font without any plain component ( NO_PROTOTYPE ). add_component(layer, shape) , INSIDE mutate of the caller's history.commit(..., operation="geometry") : it adds one built shape to the target layer and checks that the layer holds one more component of that base. Declare the target layers and glyphs in the commit. The caller's commit is then the ONE Undo step of the edit. NEW glyphs get their components another way: put them in the glyph's own Add Glyph data ( glyph_creation.NewGlyph(components=(Part(...), ...)) ). That works also in a font without any component, and each new glyph is its own Undo step with its components. Why no scratch glyph: a temporary glyph made with fontpr set_glyph adds an Add Glyph Undo step, and flPackage.deleteGlyph removes it outside history, so Redo would put the temporary glyph back ( flcommands.cpp:914,919 ). That path is a native milestone candidate, not shipped behaviour. The cost: an existing glyph in a font without any plain component is refused. Prototype filter: a clone copies the builder state (attached flag, attach anchor, component variation; flcompositeshapesbuilder.cpp:79-93 ) and the shape style (excluded, content lock, non-spacing, boolean operation, opacity; flshape.cpp:1906-1934,2213 ). An attached clone gets its offset overwritten at the next layer update ( fllayer.cpp:1493-1535 ). So a prototype qualifies only when every one of these reads as the default through Python; _qualifies holds the rules: the bound flShape members ( pyflshape.cpp:438-443 ): excluded is the bool False , opacity is 1.0 ( contentLocked is not read: it is True for every component on FontLab 9.0.9808, 504 of 504 in plum, A2 report 18, so it cannot tell a user lock; the VFJ locked key below does); the fontpr get_glyph VFJ of its glyph ( mcptools_source.cpp:58-79 , a bound Python call; no flShape member reads these fields): the layer's elements match the layer shapes one to one; the element of the prototype has no locked , nonSpacing , booleanOperation , opacity or excluded key with a non-default value, and its component holds only glyphName , layerName and attached: false (no attachAnchor , no off2026Variation ; tags of bin_types.cpp:383,535-545 ; writers flshape.cpp:826-831 , flcompositeshapesbuilder.cpp:1141-1170 ). text: Shared plan, eject and write kernel of the component writer scripts. What: the Components writer scripts (Align By Anchor, Build From Recipes, Copy Offsets Between Masters, Decompose, Nested Finder, Replace Reference, Unlock Lock) share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows. A row can hold one edit, which the script's Editor writes: EjectEditor (Decompose, Nested Finder) replaces a component with the parts of its base glyph, one level per press; MoveEditor (Align By Anchor, Copy Offsets) sets the offset of a component that plain_move accepts; other scripts subclass Editor . collect runs the planner on every editable layer and returns a Plan . Auto layers are listed and skipped, never edited. copy_problem gives the reason why the parts of a component cannot be copied safely, or "". It walks every base level as FontLab's builder does: a plain (not auto) base layer, affine transforms only, no composite shape that is not a component, no loop, not deeper than MAX_DEPTH . require_safe refuses the whole batch before any history exists: a glyph that owns an auto layer or is a base of one (also through other composites). apply_work writes all edits through ONE history.commit with operation="geometry" . EjectEditor builds the copies first, gives each removed component with its data and builder as retain= ( history.component_history ), and reads the layers back. How: eject refreshes the component cache, then copies the base parts with ejectTo() BEFORE history opens. keep_raw_state copies back what a native copy drops: the raw node connection bits (FontLab issue 8516), the element note (FontLab issue 8538) and the element name. Inside history, the write only removes the component and inserts the copies at its place. history.commit puts the retained objects first in the notification and asks for deep history, which FontLab's Undo needs for a removed component (FontLab issue 7641). Why: the logic was a private copy in each script. One App module keeps the refusals and the Undo protocol the same in every script that uses it. The generic kernel ( Change , Plan , Editor , apply_work , fmt , plural , layer_of , shown , settle ) lives in fontlabapp.masters.layers.writer ; this module re-exports it, so the Components scripts keep one import. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( history , edit_guards , layer_writer ) at load time. The fontlab module loads inside the functions, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.components.writer as component_writer def planner(glyph, master, layer): rows = [] for shape in component_writer.components(layer): why = component_writer.copy_problem( package, (glyph.name, master), shape, master ) edit = None if why else shape.id name = component_writer.base_of(shape) rows.append(component_writer.Change(name, "", "parts", edit, why)) return rows plan = component_writer.collect(glyphs, masters, planner) facts = history.scan_auto_facts(package) component_writer.require_safe(plan.work, facts) component_writer.apply_work( plan.work, "Decompose", facts, component_writer.EjectEditor(unlock=True) )

An empty componentLayer names the owner master: layer.name when it is in package.masters , else package.master (so a shown mask or brace layer uses the current master). A non-empty name applies only to its own reference. A cycle (by glyph name, so a reference to another layer of the same glyph is refused too), a nesting deeper than MAX_DEPTH , a non-affine transform or a missing base or layer skips that component; each base is reported once.
